assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson is the clearest experimental clue from nature in modern fundamental physics. It closed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and gave a concrete anchor for all later thinking about naturalness and what lies beyond. The discovery is original in execution, with instruments and analyses of unprecedented scale, and its impact is permanent.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experimental side is the natural remaining half. The difficulty is that the discovery belongs to two collaborations of thousands. The supplied credit names four people tied to the founding and leadership of ATLAS and CMS. I propose Gianotti, Della Negra and Virdee as leaders spanning both experiments. Peter Jenni is an equally defensible founder of ATLAS, so the choice is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. Both experiments independently confirmed the particle in 2012, and measurements of its couplings have since matured. Recognition is, if anything, overdue relative to the discovery.
uncertainties: Whether a three-person cap can fairly represent two collaborations, and which ATLAS or CMS leaders are most decisive, is unresolved.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history of the leadership roles and have not independently verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mapping the acoustic peaks and anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background turned cosmology into a precision science. It fixed the age, geometry and composition of the universe, including the dark energy and dark matter fractions, and it is directly relevant to the largest open questions in my field. The impact is deep and lasting.
assessment.attribution: WMAP's leadership (Bennett as PI, Page and Spergel as central figures) gives a coherent three-person configuration. Credit is complicated by the earlier 2006 prize for COBE, by Planck and ground and balloon experiments, and by the theoretical side (Sunyaev and others in the supplied list). Puget and Sunyaev make strong cases on the Planck and theory side, so any trio omits deserving people.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. WMAP and Planck confirm one another with exquisite consistency, and the LambdaCDM interpretation is stable. The tensions that exist (for example the Hubble tension) do not affect the acoustic-peak discovery itself.
uncertainties: Overlap with the COBE prize may make the committee reluctant to honour the CMB again.
Fair division among WMAP, Planck and theory credit is genuinely disputable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging the shadow of a black hole at horizon scale gives direct observational access to strong-field gravity and is a vivid existential result for our understanding of nature. It combines decades of very-long-baseline interferometry development with a concrete test of general relativity. Importance and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT collaboration, and Zensus built the European VLBI base and the mm-VLBI effort. This is a plausible three-person configuration, though the EHT is a large collaboration and contributors in modelling and VLBI technique could dispute it.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The M87* image (2019) and the Sgr A* image (2022) are independent targets, and polarisation and time-variable results are coming in. The strong-field tests are still of limited precision, so the long-term scientific payoff is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the main insight is the imaging technique or the physics outcome is a question for the committee.
Credit among collaboration leaders is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new messenger channel and, with the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and later Galactic-plane and NGC 1068 results, began to identify cosmic-ray accelerators. It is a genuine discovery from nature, achieved with an unusual instrument.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube, and Karle is a leading figure of the detector's construction and the discovery analysis. Both names are supplied and form a compact configuration. A third name from the wider collaboration could be considered but none is supplied.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature. The diffuse flux is established at high significance, and source associations have improved, though the sources of most events remain unknown. This is timely given the progress of the last several years.
uncertainties: The identity of the sources is only partly understood.
The role of KM3NeT and other efforts, and of Antarctic predecessors such as AMANDA, is not weighed in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, delivers fractional uncertainties in the 10^-18 range and enables tests of fundamental constants, gravitational redshift at millimetre scales and a path to redefining the second. It is a clean, original and highly consequential invention.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group pushed the clock to record accuracy and many-body regimes. The two names give a clean allocation. Contributors on Sr and Yb clock work (for example Lemonde, and NIST ion-clock groups) will have to be left out or recognised in passing.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance and international clock comparisons are routine. Previous prizes honoured the frequency comb (2005) and ion clocks (2012), so timing for the lattice clock fits.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier time-and-frequency prizes may reduce the sense of novelty.
The final shape of the redefinition of the second is still in progress.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a large field of moire materials. It is a clear case of theory followed quickly by decisive experiment, and it is original and transformative for condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands in 2011 and Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery. The three-person division of one theory pair and one experimental lead is natural. Cory Dean, Dmitri Efetov and others contributed key independent experiments and are left outside the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for its age. The phenomena have been reproduced in many laboratories, though the microscopic mechanism of superconductivity is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable.
uncertainties: Recognition may be a few years early compared with the long-term consolidation of the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens the low-frequency gravitational-wave window and is a direct clue from nature that touches on supermassive black hole binaries and perhaps new physics. The scientific stakes are high.
assessment.attribution: The result is the product of NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA and IPTA, with decades of pulsar timing by Manchester, Kramer and McLaughlin. Siemens leads in the NANOGrav analyses. Any three-person set leaves out important participants, so the configuration is fragile.
assessment.maturity: Premature. The 2023 evidence is at roughly the 3 to 4 sigma level, with the Hellings-Downs correlation not yet at decisive significance, and the astrophysical origin (black hole binaries versus new physics) is open. I would want more data before acting.
uncertainties: Statistical significance is not yet at discovery level.
The source of the signal is not determined.
Attribution among four large collaborations is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter in optical lattices, including the superfluid-to-Mott transition in a controlled lattice and microscope-resolved single-site imaging, gave a new experimental tool for many-body physics. It is a substantial and well-demonstrated achievement that links cold atoms to condensed-matter questions.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) provided the theoretical proposals, Greiner and Bloch carried out the decisive experiments. The supplied three-name set is coherent. Omitted are Jaksch, Cirac and Hänsch, plus the Mott-transition authors, so credit is not completely clean.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The results have been reproduced and extended widely, and quantum simulation is a standard approach. However, the field has had earlier prizes in cold atoms (BEC 2001, trapped atoms 1997 and 2012), and the practical scientific payoff for physics beyond simulation is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier cold-atom prizes and the competing Rydberg-array program.
The wider impact on unsolved problems such as high-Tc is yet to be shown.
